correctness.rationale: Relative to the uniform fixed-K measure, the special edge changes the density adjoint on 1+c h by [(p-q)-c(p+q-2)]h. The symmetric part sends h to the difference of the neighbor sums of the two occupations; for twins this equals -(k+2)h. Solving gives the positive normalized density, unique by irreducibility. Conversely c cannot be zero (h is nonzero somewhere in every intermediate sector), and the residual forces the symmetric part to send h to a scalar multiple of h. A homogeneous linear form identically zero on the K-subsets has equal coefficients by comparing subsets differing by a swap, and they must be zero since K>0. The unmarked coefficients give equality of neighbor indicators, including at K=1 and N-1. The 10 and 01 probabilities are B(1-c) and B(1+c), the ordinary currents are mean occupation differences, and the triangle contributions add to kBc on the common driven edge. Pairing configurations under u-v swap proves the marginal claim and E_mu|h|=2B gives TV. Stationarity cancels the probability logarithms in EPR; k is positive by connectedness, and (p-q)log(p/q)>0. On K_N at fixed p,q and K/N→rho in (0,1), k=N-2 and these formulas give the stated limits. An independent integer affine-residual calculation at rates 7/5 and 2/5 solved for any coefficient over 17,010 sectors/edges on the 770 labeled connected graphs of orders 3–5; it gave precisely 1,598 true-twin cases and matched their driven currents. Frozen verify.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not executed. Their broader finite checks include numerical logarithms for EPR and are not an infinite proof.
